title: The Podcast: Trying to Save the World Is No Excuse

illustration.alt: Silvia Killingsworth and a co-host record the Money Stuff podcast beside 100 John Doe name cards and paired option-and-hedge slips.

elementaryChecklist.financialMechanism: Options market makers use offsetting trades to hedge the financial risk they take when buying and selling options; the episode also discusses pensions, 401(k)s, and psychological liquidity mismatches.
elementaryChecklist.centralJoke: A serious finance podcast somehow features Susquehanna’s mysterious crowd of 100 people all called John Doe, alongside nervous frontier-pacing and the question of whether AI will write about AI.

preschool.title: One Hundred John Does and a Microphone
preschool.lesson: Options market makers hedge by taking offsetting positions to reduce the risk created when they buy and sell options.
paragraphs:
Late summer lingered; nostalgia drew near,
when Money Stuff’s new podcast arrived for your ear.
Silvia Killingsworth guest-hosted once more,
with a bundle of curious questions to explore.

There were Susquehanna’s 100 John Does—
a hundred unknowns in astonishing rows.
Then options market makers entered the chat,
buying and selling contracts this way and that.

An option gives someone a choice for a price;
a market maker helps trades happen quickly and nice.
To hedge all that risk, the maker can trade
an offsetting position, so danger may fade.

They paced at the frontier, both nervous and slow,
and asked if AI training should ease up and grow
less quickly—for economic good, or so humans survive.
Then: Who writes about AI when AI starts to write?

They discussed how money can feel near yet stay stuck,
then pensions and 401(k)s entered their luck.
The episode reached Apple and Spotify too,
with many strange questions packed into one queue.

What happened? Money Stuff released a podcast episode with guest co-host Silvia Killingsworth covering Susquehanna’s 100 John Does, options-market-making hedges, slower AI training, psychological liquidity mismatches, and putting pensions back into 401(k)s. It was distributed through Apple, Spotify, and other podcast services.
